Archlinux removed the [gdk loader from librsvg](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/librsvg/-/commits/main) because GNOME wants people to use glycin which is massive and depends on bubblewrap. 

This package restores the pixbuf loader so it needs to be added to the list of debloated packages as `librsvg-mini`

Funny enough this recent change seems to only break GTK3 apps, because I tested ghostty (GTK4) on my fork and svg icons work despite the loader being missing.


---

NOTE: I previously told Ivan that the librsvg change was rolled back, but I was wrong, I was confused by this commit message [which restores a dependency to gdk-pixbuf](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/librsvg/-/commit/a0207005edb20d1a144e3fc8a51d7bf32ace056f) but the loader is still removed.

> Funny enough this recent change seems to only break GTK3 apps, because I tested ghostty (GTK4) on my fork and svg icons work despite the loader being missing.

I don't see the point with WOW64 wine here. 

The AUR package lists the 32bit dependencies as optional already.
Bottles does not bundles WINE, it downloads its own "wine" named "soda" (a different drink lol) that does not ships 32bit libraries. This is why I need to bundle them, to run 32bit Windows programs.

I experimented setting the `ICU_DATA_FILTER_FILE` to a json that filters what to build but did not work at all, the final library was still 30 MIB...

Someone else ran into the same issue: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76326556/yocto-reducing-libicudata-size

> Bottles does not bundles WINE, it downloads its own "wine" named "soda" (a different drink lol) that does not ships 32bit libraries. This is why I need to bundle them, to run 32bit Windows programs.

Yeah they will eventually have to migrate to WOW64 anyway, because [not even the flatpak runtimes are going to be keeping 32bit libraries.](https://www.phoronix.com/news/GNOME-Flatpak-Drops-32-bit)

> Is it possible some makepkg options are screwing things up?

here is the build flags that makepkg uses for x86_64 and aarch64:

```shell
CARCH="x86_64"
CHOST="x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"

#NPROC=2

#-- Compiler and Linker Flags
#CPPFLAGS=""
CFLAGS="-march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -O2 -pipe -fno-plt -fexceptions \
         -Wformat -Werror=format-security \
         -fcf-protection \
        -fomit-frame-pointer "
CXXFLAGS="$CFLAGS -Wp,-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS"
LDFLAGS="-Wl,-O1 -Wl,--sort-common -Wl,--as-needed -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now \
         -Wl,-z,pack-relative-relocs"
LTOFLAGS="-flto=auto"
#-- Make Flags: change this for DistCC/SMP systems
MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)"
#-- Debugging flags
DEBUG_CFLAGS="-g0"
DEBUG_CXXFLAGS="$DEBUG_CFLAGS"
```

```shell
CARCH="aarch64"
CHOST="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"

#NPROC=2

#-- Compiler and Linker Flags
# -march (or -mcpu) builds exclusively for an architecture
# -mtune optimizes for an architecture, but builds for whole processor family
CPPFLAGS=""
CFLAGS="-march=armv8-a  -O2 -pipe -fstack-protector-strong -fno-plt -fexceptions \
         -Wformat -Werror=format-security \
         \
        -fomit-frame-pointer"
CXXFLAGS="$CFLAGS -Wp,-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS"
LDFLAGS="-Wl,-O1 -Wl,--sort-common -Wl,--as-needed -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now \
         -Wl,-z,pack-relative-relocs"
LTOFLAGS=""
#-- Make Flags: change this for DistCC/SMP systems
MAKEFLAGS="-j$(nproc)"
#-- Debugging flags
DEBUG_CFLAGS="-g0"
DEBUG_CXXFLAGS="$DEBUG_CFLAGS"
```

```shell
CXXFLAGS="$CFLAGS -Wp,-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS"

DEBUG_CXXFLAGS="$DEBUG_CFLAGS"
DEBUG_RUSTFLAGS="-C debuginfo=2"
```
